flawed_step: The implication fails: a unique minimum cut fixes flow only on the cut arcs, while flow downstream of the cut can be routed along alternative paths.
counterexample: V={s,a,b,t}; arcs s->a cap 1, a->t cap 5, a->b cap 1, b->t cap 5. Cuts: {s}=1, {s,a}=6, {s,b}=6, {s,a,b}=10, so {s} is the unique min cut (value 1). Max flows of value 1: f1 = (s->a:1, a->t:1, a->b:0, b->t:0); f2 = (s->a:1, a->b:1, b->t:1, a->t:0). Both satisfy capacities and conservation at a and b, and they differ on a->t, so there are two distinct maximum flows.
assessment_summary: Explicit 4-vertex network with integer capacities where {s} is the unique minimum cut (capacity 1), but value-1 flow can go s->a->t or s->a->b->t, giving distinct (indeed infinitely many) maximum flows. Statement is false.
